title: Reflection induction for predicates on roots
statement: Let $\mathcal R$ be a reduced crystallographic root pairing over $\mathbf Q$ with finite index set $I$, in the sense of Mathlib $\operatorname{RootPairing}$. Thus its roots $a_i\in M$ and coroots $a_i^\vee\in N$ lie in paired rational vector spaces [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], are injectively indexed by $I$, satisfy $\langle a_i,a_i^\vee\rangle=2$, and have integer mutual pairings, with the paired root reflections permuting both families. Let $b:\mathcal R.\operatorname{Base}$ be a base: its finite support $J\subset I$ has linearly independent roots and coroots, and every root, respectively coroot, or its negative is a nonnegative integer combination of those indexed by $J$. Write $r_j(i)$ for the index determined by $a_{r_j(i)}=a_i-\langle a_i,a_j^\vee\rangle a_j$. For any predicate $Q$ on $I$, assume $Q(i)\Rightarrow Q(r_i(i))$ for every $i$, $Q(j)$ for every $j\in J$, and $Q(i)\Rightarrow Q(r_j(i))$ whenever $j\in J$. Then $Q(i)$ for every $i\in I$. The finite index set and the base may be empty.
